subject: Private Offer - approver mapping & term phasing for multi-region pilot
messages:

Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer questions + approver list

Jonas —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Procurement has the attached draft PO and a couple questions before we route internally:

1) Buyer approvals: our procurement team will sign but finance (CFO) needs to approve >$250k TCV and our security team needs an attest for data residency if any logging is involved. Can you confirm the recommended approver slate on your side (for activation + billing)?

2) Term preference: our pilot stakeholders are split between 12-month and month-to-month pricing. Is there a standard way Redwood structures a 3-month pilot that auto-converts to a 12-month commit? Any recommended phrasing for the PO to make approvals smoother?

3) Pricing cadence: we need clarity on whether the private offer will be billed monthly based on usage or prepaid commit. We expect to start low (pilot) and ramp to ~$40k/mo for prod.

4) Timeline: procurement would like a MAP (mutual action plan) showing signature windows and activation steps — can you share a 2-week activation MAP?

Attached: AMHealth_PO_Draft_v1.pdf

Thanks — appreciate a short reply so we can circulate to finance/security this morning.

— Jacob

Hi Jacob — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vanessa (account lead), Neha (legal & finance ops), and Vivek (co-sell/regional) so we can get you a concise MAP and approver mapping. See answers below — high-level now, we can bake into the PO language once you confirm: 

1) Approver slate (recommended):
- Procurement (you) — execution
- Finance (CFO) — approval if TCV > $250k (internal threshold you mentioned)
- IT Security — attestation on logging/data residency; Redwood will provide the SOC2 report and a short evidence pack (we can add that as an attachment on activation)
- Redwood ops — activation owner (Redwood will assign an activation PM once signed)

2) Term structure option we recommend:
- Create a 3-month pilot term with monthly usage billing and an explicit conversion clause: “Upon successful completion of pilot (mutually agreed acceptance criteria), pilot will convert to a 12-month committed term at negotiated rates.”
- If procurement prefers prepaid credits for predictability, we can structure a 3-month prepaid pilot that locks in pricing and counts toward the 12-month commit if converted.

3) Pricing cadence:
- For pilots we usually bill monthly on usage. If you want to cap spend for the pilot, we can add a monthly cap. For conversion to prod we recommend an annual commitment invoiced monthly or prepaid (your call).

4) MAP (2-week fast path):
Week 0 (sign-off): procurement & finance sign PO -> Redwood sends activation questionnaire
Day 1-3: Security review (we provide SOC2 + evidence pack)
Day 3-7: Activation & provisioning (pilot infra)
Day 7-14: Pilot run + acceptance check-in -> convert to commit or end pilot

I’ll have Vanessa send a version of that MAP with timeline bullets and DocuSign/HubSpot links. Neha — can you confirm we’re comfortable with the proposed conversion clause language and whether legal prefers prepaid language?

Jacob — I attached Redwood’s private-offer term summary for quick reference.

Best,
Jonas

--

- Redwood: Sales (Jonas) = deal owner; Finance Ops (Neha) = billing & activation sign-off; Legal (cc'd on DocuSign when needed)

DocuSign/HubSpot links: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deal/RWI-8421 | DocuSign: https://docusign.com/link/xyz123 (internal routing will include Neha for invoice terms)
